newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistan newspapers - December 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistan newspapers - December 28.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Caretaker Prime Minister Malik Meraj Khalid has said more corruption cases will be instituted against past rulers within the next few days on the basis of evidence already collected.
- The size of ministries and divisions are expected to be further reduced in order to cut wasteful expenditure.
- The government is likely to raise natural gas charges between 15 to 25 percent for domestic, commercial and industrial consumers.

- All the vegetable ghee manufacturing units in Karachi have closed down their operations practically, because of the suspension of the edible oil supplies due to oil tankers' strike which entered the 22nd day on Friday.
- In order to control financial losses Pakistan Railways has suspended services of 70 trains on Fridays with effect from December 27.
- Petroleum and Natural Resources Minister Javed Jabbar has said that Pakistan has gas reserves for next 25 to 30 years if these are used with proper care and due planning.
- The LASMO Oil Company has requested the government to finalise its three pending petroleum concession agreements including one for offshore exploration.
- The government has decided to disband the government-run Punjab Road Transport Corporation.
- Afghan Taleban militiamen on Friday publicly excuted a 35-year-old Afghan, who was prosecuted and condemned for killing four people in Adreskan district of Afghanistan.
